key_insight: Under class imbalance, standard uncertainty scores can track class membership rather than ambiguity, undermining the safety of selective prediction.
clinical_relevance: Threshold-aligned uncertainty and class-stratified evaluation may help clinical AI defer ambiguous cases without disproportionately excluding minority-outcome patients.
method: Evaluated selective prediction across varying degrees of class imbalance.
Compared standard uncertainty measures with threshold-aware alternatives.
Combined CCR with threshold-aware metrics to restore within-class monotonicity.
evidence_signal: Across 56 synthetic conditions and three neurodegenerative cohorts covering multiple sclerosis, Parkinson’s disease, and Alzheimer’s disease, the proposed framework maintained bounded, balanced risk under the evaluated conditions.
watch_item: The reported evaluations do not establish prospective clinical safety; implementation requires validating thresholds and class-specific risk in the intended population.
paper_title: When uncertainty quantification fails: structural vulnerabilities and corrections for selective prediction under clinical class imbalance
